cues.en: The videos so far in this section have focused on the linguistic and what we might call cognitive capabilities of models.
cues.zh: 本章到目前，聚焦模型的語言，以及可稱為認知的能力。

cues.en: But these models don't exist in bubbles.
cues.zh: 但模型不活在泡泡裡。

cues.en: They interact with the real world, and if models are increasingly used to make decisions that impact
cues.zh: 它們與真實世界互動；越來越常用來做出影響

cues.en: real people in the real world, we want these models to be fair and unbiased.
cues.zh: 真實人類的決策時，我們希望公平、沒有偏見。

cues.en: We certainly do not want these models to be sexist or racist, or to have any other built in biases
cues.zh: 當然不希望模型有性別、種族歧視，或其他內建偏見，

cues.en: against particular genders or groups of people or nationalities.
cues.zh: 針對特定性別、群體或國籍。

cues.en: Assessing bias and fairness is actually quite tricky, and sometimes it's best done qualitatively by
cues.zh: 評估偏見與公平其實很棘手，有時最好用質性方式，

cues.en: having people read the output of a generative model and give detailed feedback about its biases.
cues.zh: 請人閱讀生成輸出，詳細回饋偏見。

cues.en: But there are some quantitative Evaluations that can give some insight into biases in language models.
cues.zh: 但有些量化評估，也能提供洞見。

cues.en: And I'm going to describe a few of those in this video.
cues.zh: 這支會描述幾種。

cues.en: But first I just want to stress that the models are not intrinsically biased against any particular social or political groups.
cues.zh: 先強調，模型本身並非天生針對特定社會或政治群體有偏見。

cues.en: Any biases or systematic unfairness in a language model comes from its training data, which means it
cues.zh: 任何偏見、系統性不公平，都來自訓練資料，也就是

cues.en: comes from the sum total of the human written text on the web, in books, and so on.
cues.zh: 網路、書籍等所有人類文字的總和。

cues.en: There are lots of papers on measuring bias and fairness in language models.
cues.zh: 有很多衡量語言模型偏見與公平的論文。

cues.en: In fact, this issue and this kind of research predates the transformer architecture.
cues.zh: 事實上，研究早於 Transformer。

cues.en: It goes back several decades to when language models were really just fixed embeddings models.
cues.zh: 可追溯幾十年前，語言模型還只是固定嵌入模型時。

cues.en: So there's a whole literature on this topic.
cues.zh: 所以有完整的研究文獻。

cues.en: And here I'm just highlighting two specific review papers, just in case you were You are interested in reading more about this literature.
cues.zh: 這裡只介紹兩篇綜述，供有興趣深入閱讀。

cues.en: I am not going to go through any Python demos, because the evaluations are basically the same as what
cues.zh: 不做 Python 示範，因為評估方式基本上

cues.en: you've already seen in this section, except that the topics, the words, and the sentences are fine tuned for assessing fairness and bias.
cues.zh: 與本章看過的相同，只是主題、用詞、句子，特別針對偏見與公平設計。

cues.en: So instead, what I'm going to do is tell you about four general approaches that are used in different eval methods.
cues.zh: 改為介紹不同評估常用的四類方法。

cues.en: One approach is to look at biases that are built in to the embeddings vectors.
cues.zh: 第一，看嵌入向量內的偏見。

cues.en: So for example you can calculate the cosine similarity between these four words here.
cues.zh: 例如，計算這四個字的餘弦相似度。

cues.en: And the idea is that if man and doctor are closely related, woman and nurse are closely related, whereas
cues.zh: 如果 man 與 doctor 很接近、woman 與 nurse 很接近，

cues.en: man and nurse and woman and doctor have weak or even negative cosine similarities, then that would
cues.zh: 但 man 與 nurse、woman 與 doctor 相似度弱，甚至為負，

cues.en: provide evidence that the embeddings matrix in this model would have some gender bias.
cues.zh: 就有證據顯示，嵌入矩陣有某種性別偏見。

cues.en: Right?
cues.zh: 對吧。

cues.en: You know, built in right at the level of the token embeddings, even before those embeddings go into a language model for processing and transformation.
cues.zh: 偏見在詞元嵌入層級就已存在，甚至還沒進語言模型處理、轉換。

cues.en: Another approach would be masked token prediction.
cues.zh: 另一種是遮罩詞元預測。

cues.en: Exactly like what I showed you several videos ago.
cues.zh: 和幾支影片前一樣。

cues.en: So for example, you can present the model a sentence like she is good at or he is good at, and then a mask token.
cues.zh: 例如輸入 she is good at，或 he is good at，再接遮罩詞元。

cues.en: And then you can look at the logit values, or maybe the log softmax values for different tokens and
cues.zh: 查看不同詞元的 logits，或 log_softmax，

cues.en: see if, for example, the logit for math is higher.
cues.zh: 例如 math 的 logit，是否在

cues.en: If the sentence starts with he compared to she.
cues.zh: he 開頭時，比 she 開頭更高。

cues.en: And then we have this example here.
cues.zh: 接著是這個例子。

cues.en: This follows from the idea of hella swag, where you look at the total probability of a sentence, Given
cues.zh: 沿用 HellaSwag 的想法，看整句機率，

cues.en: that the two sentences are the same except for the gender in this case, or it could also be a race
cues.zh: 兩句只有性別不同，也可以改成種族、

cues.en: or country of origin, or a political affiliation, or something like that.
cues.zh: 國籍、政治立場等等。

cues.en: So the idea is that if the sentence associated with a biased stereotype is deemed more likely by the
cues.zh: 如果與偏頗刻板印象相關的句子，被模型認為

cues.en: model, then that is evidence for the model having a built in bias.
cues.zh: 更可能，就有模型內建偏見的證據。

cues.en: Uh, yeah.
cues.zh: 對。

cues.en: Then we have this example.
cues.zh: 再看這個。

cues.en: This is actually also just a variant of the masked token example up here.
cues.zh: 其實也是上面遮罩詞元的變體。

cues.en: So here in this example sentence we could mask out the word for the pronoun.
cues.zh: 可以遮掉例句中的代名詞。

cues.en: And if you present the model with a word or description that might be associated with one particular
cues.zh: 如果提供可能與某個性別或群體相關的

cues.en: gender or group, and then you can see which of the pronouns the model has the highest logit for.
cues.zh: 字詞、描述，再看模型認為哪個代名詞的 logit 最高。

cues.en: I think you see from these examples that quantitatively assessing social concepts like bias and fairness is actually not too difficult.
cues.zh: 從這些例子可見，量化評估偏見、公平等社會概念，其實不太難。

cues.en: It just requires some clever and tricky ways of using the assessment methods that you are already familiar with.
cues.zh: 只需巧妙運用已熟悉的評估方法。

cues.en: Once these biases are identified, they can be trained out of the model, at least to some extent.
cues.zh: 找到偏見後，至少可以透過訓練消除一部分。

cues.en: That can happen by reinforcement learning, for example, rewarding the model for generating fair and
cues.zh: 例如強化學習，獎勵公平、

cues.en: unbiased responses and giving negative feedback to the model when it generates text that has a clear bias built in.
cues.zh: 不偏頗的回答；生成明顯有偏見的文字時，給負面回饋。

cues.en: It's also possible to modify the training set.
cues.zh: 也可以修改訓練集。

cues.en: For example, let's say you have a data set that has a lot of statements about engineers and doctors being associated with men.
cues.zh: 假設資料裡有很多把工程師、醫師與男性連結的陳述。

cues.en: You can simply edit those sentences so that they have the pronoun she instead of he or woman instead
cues.zh: 可以直接把 he 改成 she，把 man 改成 woman，

cues.en: of man, and then put those altered sentences back into the training set such that the training set
cues.zh: 再把修改後句子放回訓練集，讓

cues.en: has 50% descriptions about men being engineers and doctors, and 50% about women being engineers and doctors.
cues.zh: 男性是工程師、醫師的描述占 50%，女性也占 50%。

cues.en: I guess the final point I would like to make here is that, on the one hand, many people are justifiably
cues.zh: 最後想說，一方面，許多人合理地

cues.en: concerned about using models to make important decisions that impact people and societies.
cues.zh: 擔心模型被用於影響人與社會的重要決策，

cues.en: If these models have built in biases for or against particular groups.
cues.zh: 尤其模型對某些群體有支持或反對的偏見。

cues.en: But on the other hand, I think to the extent that these biases are taken seriously and investigated
cues.zh: 但另一方面，如果認真看待、調查，

cues.en: and tried to be corrected for, there actually is a silver lining here, because the biases that the
cues.zh: 並嘗試修正，仍有正面意義，因為

cues.en: models learn reveal biases that are in the written corpus of our cultures.
cues.zh: 模型學到的偏見，揭露文化文字語料本身的偏見。

cues.en: And so I think that trying to fix the biases in the models also has a positive impact on helping make human interactions be more fair and less biased.
cues.zh: 所以我認為，修正模型偏見，也能幫助人際互動更公平、少一些偏見。
